title: EEG: 3-Stim Auditory Oddball and Rest in Parkinson's
description: EEG recordings from 25 patients with Parkinson's disease and 25 matched controls during resting state (eyes open and eyes closed) and a three-stimulus auditory oddball task. Patients were recorded twice, one week apart, once ON and once OFF dopaminergic medication, while controls were recorded once. Accelerometer data from the most tremor-affected hand are included, along with metadata spreadsheets and code to reproduce the associated paper.
methods_description: Data were collected circa 2015 at the Cognitive Rhythms and Computation Lab, University of New Mexico. Participants completed a Matlab-based three-stimulus auditory oddball task, preceded by instructed one-minute eyes-open and eyes-closed resting periods marked by triggers. An accelerometer taped to the most tremor-affected hand recorded X, Y, and Z dimensions throughout. Patients were tested ON and OFF medication in separate sessions.
